events.title: Cable One, Inc. Reported A Surprise Loss, And Analysts Have Updated Their Forecasts
events.summary: Cable One, Inc. (NYSE:CABO) reported a surprise statutory loss of US$204 per share in its second quarter, despite analysts expecting a profit. Following these results, analysts reconfirmed revenue estimates at US$1.40 billion for 2026 but now forecast a loss instead of a profit, leading to a 22% dip in the average price target to US$54.25. The company's revenues have declined over the past five years and are projected to continue declining faster than the industry average.

articles.headline: Cable One, Inc. Reported A Surprise Loss, And Analysts Have Updated Their Forecasts

events.title: Central Garden & Pet (CENT) Signals More Acquisitions After Majority Interest Deal
events.summary: Central Garden & Pet (CENT) is actively pursuing further acquisitions, having recently agreed to acquire a majority interest in TRIXIE Heimtierbedarf GmbH & Co. KG. The company views mergers and acquisitions as a core part of its long-term growth strategy, focusing on strengthening its premium pet portfolio and shifting away from lower-margin products. Management indicates that more deals are under consideration, and the balance sheet remains strong to support these future transactions.

articles.headline: Central Garden & Pet (CENT) Signals More Acquisitions After Majority Interest Deal

events.title: Dominion's 53.8 GW data center backlog and a $66.8B merger make it the utility to watch in 2026
events.summary: Dominion Energy surpassed Q2 expectations, reporting adjusted earnings of 79 cents per share, largely driven by the surging demand from data centers in Northern Virginia, which now account for 53.8 GW of contracted capacity. The company is also navigating a complex regulatory process for its $66.8 billion merger with NextEra Energy, expected to finalize in 2027. This merger, combined with Dominion's substantial data center growth, positions it as a key utility in the evolving energy sector.

articles.headline: Dominion's 53.8 GW data center backlog and a $66.8B merger make it the utility to watch in 2026
